title: 2 Kings 16
paragraphs: ¹ In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign. ² Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. Unlike David his father, he did not do what was right in the LORD's eyes. ³ He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, and even burned his own son as an offering — following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites. ⁴ He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every leafy tree. ⁵ Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up to attack Jerusalem. They besieged Ahaz but could not overpower him.

⁶ At that time, Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the Judeans out of it; the Arameans came to Elath and have lived there to this day. ⁷ Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria with this plea: "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the king of Aram and from the king of Israel, who are attacking me." ⁸ Ahaz took the silver and gold that were in the LORD's temple and in the treasuries of the royal palace and sent them as a tribute to the king of Assyria. ⁹ The king of Assyria responded — he marched against Damascus, captured it, deported its people to Kir, and put Rezin to death. ¹⁰ King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and when he saw the altar in Damascus, he sent the priest Urijah a detailed sketch and model of it, with every feature of its construction.

¹¹ Urijah the priest built an altar exactly according to all the specifications King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, completing it before King Ahaz returned. ¹² When the king arrived from Damascus and saw the altar, he stepped forward and made offerings on it. ¹³ He presented his burnt offering and grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his fellowship offerings on the altar. ¹⁴ He also moved the bronze altar that stood before the LORD — in front of the temple, between the new altar and the temple — and set it to the north of his new altar. ¹⁵ King Ahaz gave the priest Urijah these orders: "On the great altar, offer the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and grain offering, and the burnt offering and grain offering of all the people of the land, along with their drink offerings. Sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offerings and sacrifices. But the bronze altar will be for my personal use in seeking guidance."

¹⁶ Urijah the priest did exactly as King Ahaz commanded. ¹⁷ King Ahaz also stripped the side panels from the movable stands and removed the basins from them; he took down the Sea from the bronze bulls that supported it and set it on a stone pavement. ¹⁸ He removed the covered walkway for the Sabbath that had been built at the temple, and the outer royal entrance — he took these away from the LORD's temple in deference to the king of Assyria. ¹⁹ The rest of the acts of Ahaz, and everything he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? ²⁰ Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah succeeded him.
